verdict.rationale: The only on-topic first-party evidence is a deployed-crew API endpoint, POST /resume, that resumes crew execution with human feedback. This implies a pause-for-human checkpoint at the execution or task level, not an approval gate on specific sensitive tool calls. A competitor founder's comment that CrewAI lacks deterministic hooks to pause an agent adds doubt, but it is a biased opinion, not a hands-on counter-example, so it lowers confidence rather than making this disputed. Missing for 10: documented per-tool approval gating (marking specific tools as requiring human sign-off before execution), docs explaining how the approval pause works in the open-source framework, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
